appraisal_events.evidence: Among a crowd of waiters with grotesque, hypocritical faces, Aimé alone has a 'romanesque' quality, an 'air intelligent, énergique, mais respectueux,' and answers questions about his family 'avec émotion, car il était homme de famille.'
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator singles Aimé out with a warm, distinguishing portrait that elevates him well above the other, unflatteringly described restaurant staff.

appraisal_events.evidence: Noticing Rachel's lingering attention to Aimé, Saint-Loup dismisses him brusquely and warns her he is 'une des plus grandes fripouilles que la terre ait jamais portées,' while Rachel retorts, 'Voilà que ça commence, j'en étais sûre!'
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup's jealous outburst against Aimé follows immediately on the narrator's admiring description of him, so the charge reads as jealousy speaking rather than an endorsed judgment; Rachel's weary, knowing reply shows she anticipated the pattern.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator's admiring description of Aimé's distinction and warmth locally elevates him above his surroundings.
Saint-Loup's involuntary blush and brusque, jealous attack on Aimé expose his lack of composure and security whenever his mistress's attention wanders.
Rachel's weary 'j'en étais sûre' shows her anticipating and lightly deflating Saint-Loup's predictable jealousy, giving her the composed upper hand in the exchange.
